answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a staked identity registry: an agent must lock a minimum bond of copper-denominated token before it can transact, and its weight grows only slowly with stake, so spinning up a thousand cheap clones buys almost nothing. Each new identity also needs a live pulse from an independent cost source, a paid hardware attestation that is expensive to mass-produce. When a clone is caught double-signing, its whole bond is forfeited, making the price of a botnet a deep canyon of unrecoverable capital.
